raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Summary On gfx1250 with the Triton that ships in the ROCm SDK, `fuse_scale_shift_kernel` silently computed `x * scale + shift` instead of `x * (1 + scale) + shift`, dropping the identity term from adaLN modulation in every DiT block of every diffusion step. Output was wrong but plausible-looking — no crash, no warning. This gates the affected modulation math to fp32 on gfx1250 only. All other targets keep byte-identical codegen. ## Root cause The bug is in Triton's instruction encoding, not in SGLang. gfx1250 is the only target where Triton lowers bf16 elementwise math to packed `v_pk_*_bf16`; every other target promotes to fp32 first. Comparing the two Triton builds for `bf16 + 1.0`: ``` upstream 76940ad3 (fixed): v_pk_add_bf16 v1, v1, 1.0 op_sel:[0,1] ROCm SDK 4cff872c (broken): v_pk_add_bf16 v1, v1, 1.0 op_sel_hi:[1,0] ``` The inline constant `1.0` is the **fp32** pattern `0x3F800000`. Its high half `0x3F80` is bf16 `1.0`; its low half is `0x0000`. The SDK build selects the low half for `src1` in both lanes, so the addend is bf16 zero and the operation becomes a no-op. This affects `+`, `-` and `*` against any AMDGPU hardware inline float constant — `±0.5, ±1.0, ±2.0, ±4.0` — and nothing else. Ordinary literals (`1.5`, `100.0`) are encoded as a packed bf16 pair and are correct; tensor operands are correct. In this kernel `scale_constant` is exactly `1.0`, so it hit the broken case. The bug is fixed in upstream Triton, and `3865efc` (`[AMD] support gfx1250 on ROCM 10`) already moved the gfx1250 image onto a build that carries the fix (`BUILD_TRITON=1`, `TRITON_COMMIT=76940ad3`). This change keeps SGLang correct on the SDK Triton as well, so correctness no longer depends on which Triton the image happens to ship. ## Why fp32 and not `tl.full` `tl.full` looks like it should keep the constant out of the immediate, but it does not — LLVM folds the splat straight back in. Measured on the broken build: | form | result | emitted ISA | |---|---|---| | `scale_constant + scale` | wrong | `v_pk_add_bf16` + inline const | | `tl.full(...) + scale` | wrong | `v_pk_add_bf16` + inline const | | fp32 promote | **correct** | no packed bf16 immediate | fp32 promotion was the only form that produced clean ISA. It also keeps a single rounding on store, matching what the layernorm scale/shift kernels in this same file already do. ## Scope Gated behind `is_gfx1250_supported()` and passed as a `tl.constexpr`, so Triton resolves the branch at compile time — no runtime branch, and the `else` arm is the original code verbatim. NVIDIA, XPU, gfx942 and gfx950 compile to exactly what they did before, including the `tl.full` splat, so their numerics stay bit-identical. `is_gfx1250_supported()` is `lru_cache`d and returns `False` on non-HIP builds without touching CUDA. The kernel is shared by 11 DiT families, so this is not Wan-only: `wanvideo`, `causal_wanvideo`, `hunyuanvideo`, `hunyuan3d`, `qwen_image`, `glm_image`, `joy_image`, `helios`, `lingbot_world`, `longlive2`, `mova_video_dit`. They reach it through `LayerNormScaleShift` / `RMSNormScaleShift` / `ScaleResidualRMSNormScaleShift` with the default `scale_constant=1.0`. The VAE is unaffected — adaLN is a transformer construct, and an ISA scan over a full Wan2.2 run (1307 kernels, 118 using packed bf16) found this kernel as the only affected one. ## Testing After this PR is applied, the video can be played. Extracted pic comparison as below: Tested on rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.20-rocm10-mi45x-test-triton4cff872c-20260923. Existing unit test `test_scale_shift_4d_matches_torch`, run against both Triton builds: | Configuration | Result | |---|---| | ROCm SDK Triton (broken), with fix | 16 passed | | Upstream Triton (fixed), with fix | 16 passed — no regression | | ROCm SDK Triton, fix reverted | **3 failed** (the bf16 + `scale_constant=1` cases) | | ROCm SDK Triton, gate forced off | **3 failed** — confirms the `else` arm is the original path | End-to-end Wan2.2-T2V-A14B on the broken SDK Triton (720×1280, 193 frames, 8 steps, seed 42) completed cleanly and matches a known-good baseline generated on the fixed Triton: correlation **0.991**, PSNR **29.3 dB**, mean abs diff 4.3/255. A dropped identity term collapses structure, so this margin is rounding and sampling non-determinism, not lost conditioning. Performance is unchanged. `bench_scale_shift_4d.py`, 3 runs each way, medians: 117.7 vs 119.9 µs (wan), 16.23 vs 16.24 µs (longlive). Within-group spread was ±20% on the larger workloads, so those deltas are noise — the kernel reads three tensors and writes one with no reuse, so it is bandwidth-bound and the extra `v_cvt` ops hide behind memory latency. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #39266514373](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39266514373) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #39266514438](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39266514438) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #39266514463](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39266514463)

detail.title: [Fix] [AMD] bugfix: Wan2.2 crash due to Triton kernel compilation

files.patch:
@@ -15,6 +15,13 @@
 )
 from sglang.srt.utils import is_gfx1250_supported
 
+# gfx1250 only: the ROCm SDK's Triton emits packed v_pk_*_bf16 for
+# bf16 elementwise math, and that op reads an inline float immediate
+# (+-0.5/1/2/4) from the wrong half of the 32-bit word -- as zero -- silently
+# dropping the identity term in ``scale_constant + scale``. tl.full does not
+# help; the splat folds back into the immediate.
+_FP32_MODULATE = is_gfx1250_supported()
+
 
 @triton.jit
 def _fused_scaled_residual_add_exact_kernel(
@@ -289,6 +296,7 @@ def _fused_scale_shift_4d_kernel(
     num_frames,
     frame_seqlen,
     BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr,
+    FP32_MODULATE: tl.constexpr = _FP32_MODULATE,
 ):
     pid_row = tl.program_id(0)
     pid_col = tl.program_id(1)
@@ -319,6 +327,11 @@ def _fused_scale_shift_4d_kernel(
         # CuTe's residual path has no extra +0 on the gate. In particular,
         # adding +0 would change a negative-zero gate before multiplication.
         output = normalized * scale + shift
+    elif FP32_MODULATE:
+        output = normalized.to(tl.float32) * (
+            scale_constant + scale.to(tl.float32)
+        ) + shift.to(tl.float32)
+        output = output.to(out_ptrs.dtype.element_ty)
     else:
         scale_const_tensor = tl.full([BLOCK_N], scale_constant, dtype=scale.dtype)
         output = normalized * (scale_const_tensor + scale) + shift
@@ -349,6 +362,7 @@ def fuse_scale_shift_kernel_blc_opt(
     SHIFT_IS_SCALAR: tl.constexpr,
     BLOCK_L: tl.constexpr,
     BLOCK_C: tl.constexpr,
+    FP32_MODULATE: tl.constexpr = _FP32_MODULATE,
 ):
     pid_l = tl.program_id(0)
     pid_c = tl.program_id(1)
@@ -390,7 +404,14 @@ def fuse_scale_shift_kernel_blc_opt(
         )
         scale = tl.load(scale_ptr + sc_off, mask=mask, other=0)
 
-    y = x * (scale_constant + scale) + shift
+    if FP32_MODULATE:
+        y = x.to(tl.float32) * (scale_constant + scale.to(tl.float32)) + shift.to(
+            tl.float32
+        )
+        y = y.to(y_ptr.dtype.element_ty)
+    else:
+        y = x * (scale_constant + scale) + shift
+
     tl.store(y_ptr + x_off, y, mask=mask)
